report:
# Whole-Body Vibration Therapy for Fracture Prevention in Osteoporosis: The Evidence

**Bottom line: The evidence does not support WBV as an effective fracture-prevention therapy, though it may modestly help with bone density and falls.**

## What the research shows

The most direct evidence comes from a 2017 systematic review and meta-analysis (Jepsen et al.) specifically designed to assess WBV's effect on fracture risk in adults over 50 ([bmjopen.bmj.com](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/7/12/e018342)). While this review found WBV significantly improved lumbar spine bone mineral density and reduced fall rates, it did not find robust evidence for direct fracture prevention — the authors themselves noted the fracture data was limited, stating WBV "may prevent fractures by reducing falls" rather than through a direct skeletal mechanism ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29289937](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29289937/)).

A more recent 2025 critique reinforces skepticism about even the falls-prevention claims. Authors affiliated with Cochrane Collaboration falls-prevention reviews challenged a Canadian Task Force conclusion of "moderate-certainty evidence" for WBV, arguing the evidence base is weaker than portrayed ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12577057](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12577057/); [link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13643-025-02946-5](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13643-025-02946-5)).

Separately, bone-density-focused meta-analyses (e.g., 2022 Springer review) show statistically significant but small improvements in BMD with WBV in postmenopausal women ([link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-022-06556-y](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-022-06556-y)) — but improved BMD does not automatically translate into reduced fracture incidence, and no trial has been adequately powered to measure fractures as a primary endpoint.

## Conclusion

Current evidence is insufficient to confirm WBV prevents fractures. Benefits are limited to modest BMD gains and possible fall reduction, with experts actively disputing even the falls evidence. Larger, fracture-endpoint-specific trials are needed before WBV can be considered an effective osteoporosis fracture-prevention intervention.
